title: Bare `uv run --project pipeline pytest` from the repo root runs the live ingest test
body:
## Summary
pipeline/pyproject.toml deselects `live` tests via addopts, but pytest reads that config only when it is the rootdir's; the documented gate run from the repo root loaded no config and ran test_live_lane1_end_to_end - a real f1db ingest into data/raw.

## Description
`addopts = "-m 'not live'"` (pipeline/pyproject.toml:31) is the only thing keeping test_live_lane1_end_to_end (pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:187) offline. The command written in .ai/manifest.yaml:16 (`pipeline-test`), .claude/scan-sweep/config.md:21 and .claude/perfect/config.md:31 is `uv run --project pipeline pytest` with no path; from the repo root pytest finds no ini in the cwd's ancestors, so rootdir is the repo root, no addopts apply, and the marker is even reported unknown. `just test` / `pnpm check` pass `pipeline/tests` (and check.mjs adds `-m "not live"`), so they were safe; the documented bare command was not. Fixed (technique: test-harness/derived-selection-must-be-measured): pipeline/tests/conftest.py registers the `live` marker and deselects live items unless the -m expression names `live` positively, independent of which config loaded.

## Flow
- run `uv run --project pipeline pytest` from the repo root (this round's gate run, 2026-10-04 15:02)
- no config -> live test collected -> EthicalClient with the owner contact -> 5 polite requests to api.github.com / release-assets.githubusercontent.com
- new raw snapshot data/raw/f1db/2026-10-04T130259Z (release v2026.16.0), `current` moved from 2026-09-29T190615Z
- fix: conftest hook deselects live tests; `-m live` (just e2e-live) still selects them

## Expected impact
Every agent or owner who runs the documented pipeline gate stops spending GitHub quota, waiting ~6 min on 120 s spacing and moving the raw `current` pointer. Could break: nothing that runs live tests deliberately - `-m live` still selects them.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the offline gate can no longer perform a live ingest
Before: repo-root `--collect-only`: 124 collected incl. test_live_lane1_end_to_end, PytestUnknownMarkWarning; the real run fetched 4.49 MB and wrote a snapshot
After: 133/134 collected (1 deselected), no warning; bare gate run 150 passed, 1 deselected, no new snapshot; `-m live` -> 1/134 selected
Method: gate - test_live_guard.py runs a synthetic live test (writes a sentinel) under an empty pytest.ini; seeded red by renaming the hooks (1 failed, sentinel written), green after (10 passed)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/pyproject.toml:31 addopts = "-m 'not live'"
.ai/manifest.yaml:16 pipeline-test: uv run --project pipeline pytest
run 2026-10-04: 1 failed (test_live_lane1_end_to_end), 60 passed in 389.50s; PytestUnknownMarkWarning at test_lane1_e2e.py:187
data/raw/f1db/fetch_log.jsonl: robots 404, releases/latest 200, assets/609802005 302, release-assets robots 404, blob 200 4490752 B

title: run_transform leaks STATREEL_WAREHOUSE and F1DB_SNAPSHOT into os.environ
body:
## Summary
run_transform wrote the dbt env into the calling process's os.environ, so every later Paths() resolved the previous run's warehouse.

## Description
pipeline/statreel_ingest/transform.py:46-47 did `os.environ.update(...)` and `os.environ["STATREEL_WAREHOUSE"] = ...`; Paths.warehouse's default factory reads STATREEL_WAREHOUSE (pipeline/statreel_ingest/config.py:24). One rule (which warehouse) had two writers. Fixed: the env is built as a dict and passed to run_dbt's child only (transform.py run_dbt(env=...)).

## Flow
- replay_run fixture runs run_transform on a pytest tmp warehouse (test_lane1_e2e.py:104)
- later in the same process the live test builds Paths() -> warehouse = the tmp file the fixture still holds open
- dbt: "Cannot open file ...pytest-202\lane10\warehouse.duckdb: being used by another process" (pipeline/dbt/logs/dbt.log:4254)

## Expected impact
Any process that transforms twice (tests, a future in-process runner) gets the right warehouse. Could break: nothing reads os.environ after the call.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one process-wide setting no longer silently follows the last transform
Before: after run_transform, os.environ carries both keys; test_transform.py red on HEAD
After: dbt's env carries both, os.environ neither, a fresh Paths() keeps its default; lane1 replay 31 passed
Method: gate - test_transform.py monkeypatches run_dbt to capture its env; red on HEAD, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/statreel_ingest/transform.py:46 os.environ.update(_snapshot_env(paths))
pipeline/statreel_ingest/transform.py:47 os.environ["STATREEL_WAREHOUSE"] = paths.warehouse.as_posix()
pipeline/statreel_ingest/config.py:24 warehouse default_factory reads STATREEL_WAREHOUSE

title: Transport failures leave no row in the fetch log
body:
## Summary
A timeout or refused connection raised out of EthicalClient._send before _log, and an unreachable robots.txt was turned into 'disallow' without a row.

## Description
client.py's docstring and DESIGN §5.2 promise every fetch is logged. pipeline/statreel_ingest/client.py:128 called _http.get then _log - an httpx.HTTPError skipped the log; _fetch_robots caught HTTPError and returned None silently. The failure most needing evidence (an outage vs a block - technique web-scraping/shape-change-detection: tell collapse apart from block and outage by the acquire stage's evidence) left none. Fixed: both paths log status null + the error class, then fail as before.

## Flow
- mock transport raises ReadTimeout on a data URL / ConnectError on robots.txt
- before: no row for either; after: one row each with status null and error ReadTimeout|ConnectError

## Expected impact
The owner reading fetch_log.jsonl after a failed `just ingest` can see which host failed and how. Could break: a log reader expecting int status - none exists (grep).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - failed fetches are evidenced
Before: 0 rows for 2 failure paths (2 new tests red on HEAD)
After: 1 row each
Method: gate - 2 tests in test_client.py, red then green; 52 passed across client/politeness/f1db/guard
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/statreel_ingest/client.py:128 resp = self._http.get(url, headers=headers)  # raises before _log
pipeline/statreel_ingest/client.py:189 except httpx.HTTPError: return None  # no row

title: A snapshot's fetch_log.jsonl carries every earlier run's fetches
body:
## Summary
f1db.ingest copied the client's cumulative log into each snapshot, so a snapshot's provenance listed requests from previous runs.

## Description
DESIGN §5.2: every fetch logged to data/raw/<source>/<snapshot>/fetch_log.jsonl. The client log is data/raw/f1db/fetch_log.jsonl, appended across runs (cli.py:27); pipeline/statreel_ingest/sources/f1db.py:93 did shutil.copyfile of the whole file. Fixed: the ingest records the log's size before its first request and copies only the bytes appended since.

## Flow
- two ingests (v1, v2) with the same client log
- before: snapshot 2's fetch_log repeats all of snapshot 1's rows
- after: snapshot rows partition the cumulative log

## Expected impact
Snapshot provenance states what that snapshot's run fetched. Could break: nothing reads the snapshot copy (grep).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - provenance matches its claim
Before: data/raw/f1db/2026-10-04T130259Z/fetch_log.jsonl: 14 rows, 5 its own; test red on HEAD
After: first + second == all, disjoint
Method: gate - test_each_snapshot_carries_only_its_own_fetches, red then green; 44 passed incl. lane1
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Registry accepts a rate limit of zero or below - an unthrottled client
body:
## Summary
RateLimit.requests/per_s/burst_per_s had no positivity check, so a typo produced a ZeroDivisionError or a zero/negative spacing.

## Description
Source.min_interval_s (pipeline/statreel_ingest/registry.py:65-73) divides per_s by requests and halves; `requests: 0` crashes, `per_s: 0` or a negative count yields interval <= 0 (HostThrottle never sleeps), `burst_per_s: 0` is ignored as falsy. Technique rate-limiting/limit-derivation: the number must carry its predicate. Fixed (policy-tighten): Field(gt=0) on all three.

## Flow
- sources.yaml entry with rate_limit {requests: 5, per_s: 0}
- before: loads; min_interval_s = 0
- after: Registry.load raises 'greater than 0'

## Expected impact
A malformed registry edit fails at load instead of running at full speed. Could break: an entry with a non-positive figure - none in the seed.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the throttle cannot be zeroed by data
Before: 4 of 4 malformed limits load
After: 4 of 4 rejected; seed loads, f1db still 120 s
Method: gate - parametrized test, red on HEAD, green after; 64 passed
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
pipeline/statreel_ingest/registry.py:28-31 requests: float / per_s: float / burst_per_s: float | None (no bounds)
pipeline/statreel_ingest/registry.py:70 intervals = [rl.per_s / rl.requests]

title: Unknown source and missing contact escape the CLI as tracebacks
body:
## Summary
`just ingest <typo>` raised a bare KeyError and a missing owner contact raised MissingContact out of main() - tracebacks with exit 1, unlike every other refusal (exit 3).

## Description
pipeline/statreel_ingest/cli.py:73 caught only PermissionError/BackedOff/SchemaDrift; Registry.get raised KeyError (registry.py:94), MissingContact is a ValueError (client.py:31). Fixed: UnknownSource(KeyError) with a plain str(); main() maps UnknownSource and MissingContact to 'refused: ...' and exit 3.

## Flow
- `statreel-ingest ingest no-such-source` -> before: KeyError traceback, exit 1; after: 'refused: source ... is not in the registry', exit 3
- no contact -> before: MissingContact traceback; after: refused line, exit 3, before any request

## Expected impact
Operators get one readable line and a stable exit code. Could break: callers catching KeyError still match (subclass).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - refusals are legible and consistently coded
Before: 2 of 3 refusal paths end in a traceback
After: 3 of 3 print 'refused:' and return 3
Method: gate - test_cli.py red on HEAD, green after; 70 passed
Result: better
Gate: none

pipeline/statreel_ingest/registry.py:94 raise KeyError(...)

title: Lineage marks a parentless model 'legal' with no sources
body:
## Summary
compute_lineage starts every model at 'legal', so a model with no dbt parents (core.data_snapshot) is proven legal with sources [] - against the module's own rule that unprovable lineage is 'unknown'.

## Description
pipeline/statreel_ingest/lineage.py:8-9 says anything whose lineage cannot be proven must never pass a monetized gate, but lineage.py:32 initialises cls='legal' and a node with no depends_on keeps it. data_snapshot (pipeline/dbt/models/core/data_snapshot.sql) reads the snapshot manifest via env_var with no source() ref -> ('legal', []). Fix shape: parentless models are 'unknown' unless the node declares meta {license_class, source_id}, and data_snapshot declares f1db - the second half is a dbt model file (Warehouse Transform context), so this is an out-of-scope seam.

## Flow
- compute_lineage over pipeline/dbt/target/manifest.json -> 26 models; data_snapshot = ('legal', [])
- change: lineage reads node meta for parentless nodes, else unknown; add meta to data_snapshot in _core__models.yml
- instrument: test_lineage case (parentless -> unknown; with meta -> declared) + lane1 assertion f1_data_as_of stays ('legal', ['f1db'])

## Expected impact
Publish gating stops trusting a model whose licence nobody declared. Could break: f1_data_as_of would go 'unknown' if the meta half lands without the lineage half or vice versa - they must land together.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - lineage honours its own unknown-outranks rule
Before: 1 of 26 models proven legal with zero sources
After: predicted 0 of 26 (data_snapshot declared f1db via meta)
Method: simulation - walked over the real manifest; the build needs pipeline/dbt (other context), so not gated this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/statreel_ingest/lineage.py:32 cls, ids = "legal", frozenset()
probe: NOSRC data_snapshot legal [] (26 models)
instrument: test_lineage: parentless node -> unknown, parentless with meta -> declared; lane1 test_data_as_of lineage stays ('legal', ['f1db'])

title: A robots.txt redirect is treated as a full disallow
body:
## Summary
_fetch_robots does not follow redirects, so a 3xx on /robots.txt falls into the 'None -> disallow' branch.

## Description
pipeline/statreel_ingest/client.py:183-203: 2xx parse, 4xx allow, else None (disallow). RFC 9309 §2.3.1.2 says crawlers SHOULD follow at least five redirects for robots.txt. Fail-closed today: a host that moves robots.txt (apex -> www, a CDN) becomes unreachable for the whole TTL. Following redirects - only to registered hosts, through authorize() - widens what the ethics layer will fetch, so it is policy-loosen and the owner's call.

## Flow
- source host answers /robots.txt with 301 -> https://www.host/robots.txt
- today: RobotsDisallowed for every URL on the host
- proposed: follow <= 5 hops to registered https hosts, then parse

## Expected impact
Only matters when a registered source moves its robots.txt; f1db's hosts answer 404. Could break: widens fetch surface.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - RFC 9309 conformance
Before: 3xx robots -> disallow
After: 3xx robots followed within registered hosts
Method: simulation - no registered host redirects robots.txt today
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence:
pipeline/statreel_ingest/client.py:196-203 (2xx parse / 4xx empty / else None)
pipeline/statreel_ingest/client.py:87 follow_redirects=False

title: F1 'live' capability fails every winter break
body:
## Summary
capabilities.yaml sets F1/live max_staleness_days 35, but the off-season gap is ~90 days, so the live cell goes red every January-March while the data is as fresh as it can be.

## Description
pipeline/capabilities.yaml:28-31 (comment: a race weekend every 1-3 weeks in season). Abu Dhabi 2025-12-07 -> Australia 2026-03-08 = 91 days: the check fails from ~2026-01-11 until the first race. Whether 'live' should mean 'fresh in season' (calendar-aware) or 'fresh, period' is a product definition the heatmap and season-so-far use case both read.

## Flow
- evaluate capabilities on 2026-02-01 with the real warehouse
- latest race 2025-12-07 -> 56 days > 35 -> F1/live fail
- options: calendar-aware staleness (vs next scheduled race), a seasonal threshold, or accept the red

## Expected impact
The heatmap's live cell would stop crying wolf each winter. Could break: a too-loose rule hides a real stall in season.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - capability status matches reality
Before: ~60 red days/year from calendar alone
After: 0 with a calendar-aware rule (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked over the 2025/26 calendar; no instrument decides what 'live' should mean
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
pipeline/capabilities.yaml:31 max_staleness_days: 35
pipeline/statreel_ingest/capabilities.py:52-59 staleness = today - max(race_date <= today)

title: DESIGN §5.2 states two ingest mechanisms the code does not have
body:
## Summary
DESIGN §5.2 says `access: manual` sources get a CLI import helper with a provenance note and a monthly job hashes each terms_url and blocks ingests on change; neither exists.

## Description
DESIGN.md:188 (manual CLI helper) and DESIGN.md:195 (terms monitoring: fetch each terms_url monthly, SHA-256, needs_review, block new ingests). cli.py offers ingest/transform/capabilities only; INGESTERS = {f1db} (cli.py:14); no terms hash anywhere (grep terms_hash/needs_review: 0 in pipeline). 10 registry sources are access: manual. Terms monitoring fetches terms_url hosts that are not in any source's `hosts` (e.g. github.com, www.nba.com), so building it changes what the ethics layer may fetch - an owner decision; the alternative is to state the gap in DESIGN.

## Flow
- owner reads DESIGN §5.2 and expects terms changes to block ingests
- nothing hashes terms; only the stale-terms age warning (built this round) exists
- decide: build (manual import = L; terms monitor = M + new fetch targets) or mark both 'planned' in DESIGN

## Expected impact
DESIGN stops asserting protections the code lacks. Could break: n/a.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - doc claims match code
Before: 2 stated mechanisms, 0 implemented
After: 2 implemented, or 0 claimed
Method: probe - grep over pipeline/ and the CLI surface
Result: better
Gate: direction
